sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface localization confirmed by non-permeabilized anti-FLAG staining in COS-7 cells; no functional assay reported in this clip.
sites.rationale: Non-permeabilized surface staining with an anti-FLAG antibody proves the FLAG epitope is extracellular. NRP2 topology provides exactly one extracellular terminus — the mature N-terminus beginning at residue 21 after cleavage of the 20-residue signal peptide — so the tag must be inserted after residue 20 (V20 | R21). Python verification confirms seq_dict[20]='V' and seq_dict[21]='R'. The tag is 844 residues from the TM boundary, well clear of any steric constraint. Flag-tagged full-length Nrp2 expressed in COS-7 cells; surface staining with anti-FLAG antibody on non-permeabilized cells confirmed the FLAG epitope is displayed on the plasma membrane. No residue number is stated in the clip, but NRP2 is a type I transmembrane protein: the only extracellular terminus is the mature N-terminus (residue 21 onward after signal-peptide cleavage at residue 20). A C-terminal FLAG would be cytoplasmic and invisible to non-permeabilized surface staining, so the tag must sit after the signal-peptide cleavage site, i.e., insert_after_residue = 20.

sources.claim: COS-7 cells transfected with flag-tagged wild-type Nrp2 or Nrp1 expression plasmids were subjected to surface staining with a flag antibody to visualize Nrp localization on the plasma membrane.

literature_notes: L1 and L2 are from the same paper and report the same FLAG-tagged NRP2 construct; L1 is used as the primary clip. The position is topology_derived because neither clip names a residue number — the junction is uniquely determined by the signal-peptide cleavage site (residue 20/21) and the fact that non-permeabilized surface staining proves the FLAG is extracellular, ruling out a C-terminal placement. L3 (NRP2-HA) uses the standard '-HA' C-terminal naming convention; NRP2's C-terminus (residues 889–931) is intracellular, so this is an intracellular tag and is recorded in other_positions. L4 explicitly states 'C-terminal FLAG epitope tag', which is likewise intracellular and recorded in other_positions. L5 reports Flag-tagged full-length NRP2 in HEK293 cells used in infection assays but names no tag position (N- or C-terminal unspecified); it cannot independently pin a new surface site and does not add a second site. No ledger line supports an internal extracellular loop insertion for NRP2.

literature_other_positions.note: L4 explicitly states the NRP2 ORF carries a C-terminal FLAG tag; residue 931 (A) is the last residue of the intracellular tail (889–931), so this tag faces the cytoplasm and is not a surface site.

L3 names an 'NRP2-HA' construct; the '-HA' suffix denotes a C-terminal HA tag appended after residue 931 (A), which lies in the intracellular domain (889–931) and is not accessible on the cell surface.
